title: Markets Anticipate End Of Iran War

Markets Anticipate End Of Iran War

Anatole Kaletsky

Gavekal Research | 9 Nov 2026

Why did stock markets celebrate all over the world last Wednesday and then collapse on Thursday? Why did the Republican Party suffer its biggest electoral defeat in 50 years? And what does all this mean for investment conditions in the months ahead? These three questions have provoked many fascinating and complex responses. But if a simple explanation seems sufficient, the principle of “Occam’s Razor” says we should consider it seriously, especially if there is circumstantial evidence in its support.Occam’s Razor cuts through the complexities of the election and markets with this obvious answer: last week’s Republican wipeout left Donald Trump with one way—and only one way—to achieve what must be the main objective of his lame-duck period, now that he has thoroughly enriched himself and secured personal immunity from the Supreme Court. Trump clearly craves an exalted place in US history—and he is unlikely to achieve immortality by building a new White House ballroom, or a triumphal arch that will be demolished the moment he loses power.
